title: Microsoft Purview retention: what is kept, what is deleted and who decides
summary: Held because the adaptive-scope licensing requirement excludes qualifying Office 365 and Information Protection and Governance plans, potentially prompting an unnecessary purchase. Microsoft's Copilot PowerShell reference also conflicts with the guide's example and marks the application selection as preview; the page should disclose that disagreement.

claims.claim: Purview retention policies and labels determine how long Microsoft 365 content, including Copilot interactions, is retained and when it is permanently deleted.
claims.quote: To assign your retention settings to content, use **retention policies** and **retention labels with label policies**. You can use just one of these methods, or combine them.

claims.claim: Create a retention policy at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy.
claims.quote:
**Solutions** > **Data Lifecycle Management** > **Policies** > **Retention policies**.
2. Select **New retention policy**

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy with Name, ExchangeLocation and SharePointLocation creates a policy for the specified mailboxes and sites, with a rule required separately as the note explains.
claims.quote: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name "Regulation 123 Compliance" -ExchangeLocation "Kitty Petersen", "Scott Nakamura" -SharePointLocation "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/teams/finance"

claims.claim: Copilot retention is configured through Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy.
claims.quote:
**Solutions** > **Data Lifecycle Management** > **Policies** > **Retention policies**.
2. Select **New retention policy**

claims.claim: Set-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -Applications "User:M365Copilot" adds Microsoft 365 Copilot to an existing policy for newer locations.
claims.quote: Set-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity “<policy name>” -Applications "User:M365Copilot"
claims.fix: Keep the cited guide's example, but append this note: 'The Set-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy reference marks Microsoft Copilot experiences as Preview and says all these application values must be supplied together: User:M365Copilot,CopilotForSecurity,CopilotinFabricPowerBI,CopilotStudio,CopilotinBusinessApplicationplatformsSales,SQLCopilot. This conflicts with the policy guide's single-application example.' Link that note to https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-appretentioncompliancepolicy?view=exchange-ps.

claims.claim: Create a retention label at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Retention labels > Create a label.
claims.quote:
**Solutions** > **Data Lifecycle Management** > **Retention labels**.
2. Select **Create a label**

claims.claim: New-ComplianceTag with Name, RetentionAction Keep, RetentionDuration and RetentionType ModificationAgeInDays creates the stated retention label.
claims.quote: New-ComplianceTag -Name "HR Content" -RetentionAction Keep -RetentionDuration 1825 -RetentionType ModificationAgeInDays

claims.claim: Publish labels at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Label policies > Publish labels.
claims.quote:
**Solutions** > **Data Lifecycle Management** > **Policies** > **Label policies**
2. Select **Publish labels**

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -SharePointLocation <site-url> can create the policy container for retention labels, with a label added separately as the note explains.
claims.quote: Use the New-RetentionCompliancePolicy cmdlet to create new retention policies and new retention label policies in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal.

claims.claim: Create an adaptive scope at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope.
claims.quote:
**Settings** > **Roles and scopes** > **Adaptive scopes**.
2. On the **Adaptive scopes** page, select **+ Create scope**.

claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <name> -LocationType User -RawQuery <query> creates a user adaptive scope using an advanced query.
claims.quote:
New-AdaptiveScope
    -Name <String>
    -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType>
    -RawQuery <String>

claims.claim: The Preservation Lock guide says enabling the lock is unavailable in the UI; the row supplies no UI path and explicitly flags Microsoft's conflicting checkbox documentation.
claims.quote: You must use PowerShell if you need to use Preservation Lock. Because administrators can't disable or delete a policy for retention after this lock is applied, enabling this feature is not available in the UI to safeguard against accidental configuration.

claims.claim: Set-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<Name of Policy>" -RestrictiveRetention $true applies Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: Set-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<Name of Policy>" -RestrictiveRetention $true

claims.claim: Select a policy at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies to inspect its distribution status.
claims.quote: You can always check the distribution status of the retention policy by selecting it from the **Retention policies** page in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<Name of Policy>" -DistributionDetail | Format-List provides read-only policy details including distribution information.
claims.quote: Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "Regulation 123 Compliance" -DistributionDetail | Format-List

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: A retention policy is not valid until a rule is added with New-RetentionComplianceRule.
claims.quote: Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies) or a label is added (for retention label policies). For more information, see New-RetentionComplianceRule.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot experiences retention location includes Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts and responses.
claims.quote: **Microsoft Copilot experiences**: For built-in and custom Copilot experiences, all user prompts responses. Includes Microsoft 365 Copilot, Security Copilot, Copilot in Fabric, Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: The cited Copilot command is for an existing retention policy for newer locations.
claims.quote: To add Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions to an existing retention policy for newer locations, such as Teams private channel messages and Viva Engage:

claims.claim: A retention label's name cannot be changed after it is saved.
claims.quote: Be careful what name you choose, because this can't be changed after the label is saved.

claims.claim: New-RetentionComplianceRule adds a retention label to a retention label policy.
claims.quote: The next step is to use the New-RetentionComplianceRule cmdlet to add a retention label to the retention label policy.

claims.claim: Creating adaptive scopes requires the Scope Manager role.
claims.quote: Any role group with the *Scope Manager* role can create an adaptive scope.

claims.claim: Adaptive-scope query changes can take up to five days to take effect.
claims.quote: adaptive scope query changes can take up to five days to become effective and reflected in the scope details view of the Adaptive Scopes page.

claims.claim: The Get-RegulatoryComplianceUI reference describes a preservation-lock checkbox, contrary to the lock guide's UI statement.
claims.quote: whether the preservation lock checkbox is displayed for retention policies and the immutable label checkbox is displayed for retention labels

claims.claim: RestrictiveRetention returned by Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy indicates whether Preservation Lock is set.
claims.quote:
Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<Name of Policy>" |Fl
```

You should see **RestrictiveRetention** is set to **True**.

claims.claim: Without DistributionDetail, DistributionStatus and location property values are inaccurate.
claims.quote: If you don't use this switch, the values of the DistributionStatus and \*Location property values will be inaccurate.

claims.where: What it is: opening; comparison table
claims.claim: Retention policies assign the same retention settings at container level, such as a site or mailbox.
claims.quote: assigning the same retention settings at the container level to be automatically inherited by content in that container.

claims.where: What it is: opening; comparison table
claims.claim: Retention labels assign retention settings at item level, including folders, documents and emails.
claims.quote: use a retention label to assign retention settings at an item level (folder, document, email).

claims.claim: Retain and delete actions provide retain-only, delete-only, and retain-then-delete outcomes.
claims.quote:
Retain-only: Retain content forever or for a specified period of time.
- Delete-only: Permanently delete content after a specified period of time.
- Retain and then delete: Retain content for a specified period of time and then permanently delete it.

claims.where: What it is: content stays in place
claims.claim: Retention works with content in its original location.
claims.quote: When content has retention settings assigned to it, that content remains in its original location.

claims.claim: A copy is automatically retained when users edit or delete content included in retention.
claims.quote: if they edit or delete content that's included in the retention policy, a copy of the content is automatically retained.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive retained copies are stored in the Preservation Hold library.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive sites: The copy is retained in the **Preservation Hold** library.

claims.claim: Exchange mailbox retained copies are stored in Recoverable Items.
claims.quote: For Exchange mailboxes: The copy is retained in the **Recoverable Items** folder.

claims.claim: Copies for Teams, Viva Engage messages, Copilot and AI apps are retained in the hidden SubstrateHolds folder.
claims.quote: For Teams, Viva Engage messages, Copilot and AI apps: The copy is retained in a hidden folder named **SubstrateHolds** as a subfolder in the Exchange **Recoverable Items** folder.

claims.claim: Retention settings from policies do not follow content moved outside the policy's container.
claims.quote: the retention settings don't travel with the content in its new location. If that's required, use retention labels instead of retention policies.

claims.claim: Retention label settings follow content moved within the Microsoft 365 tenant.
claims.quote: Unlike retention policies, retention settings from retention labels travel with the content if it's moved to a different location within your Microsoft 365 tenant.

claims.claim: Retention policy settings are not manually applied to individual items.
claims.quote: | Retention settings applied manually | No | Yes |

claims.claim: Retention labels can be applied manually.
claims.quote: **Enable people in your organization to apply a retention label manually** to content in Outlook and Outlook on the web, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: Adaptive scopes use a query that runs daily against selected attributes or properties.
claims.quote: dynamic by running daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected locations.

claims.claim: Static policy scope covers an entire location or specific inclusions and exclusions.
claims.quote: A **static scope** doesn't use queries and is limited in configuration in that it can apply to all instances for a specified location, or use inclusion and exclusions for specific instances for that location.

claims.where: What it is: Precedence; Risks and limits: Retention beats deletion
claims.claim: Ordinary retention takes precedence over permanent deletion, subject to the separately disclosed Priority cleanup exception.
claims.quote: By default, retention always takes precedence over permanent deletion, and the longest retention period wins.

claims.claim: The longest retention period for an item wins.
claims.quote: If content is subject to multiple retention settings that retain content for different periods of time, the content is retained until the end of the longest retention period for the item.

claims.claim: For deletion conflicts after retention is resolved, a label's delete action takes precedence over any policy's delete action.
claims.quote: a delete action from a retention label always takes precedence over a delete action from any retention policy.

claims.claim: For policy deletion conflicts, adaptive scopes or specific inclusions take precedence over a policy covering all instances of the location.
claims.quote: If a retention policy for a location uses an adaptive scope or a static scope that includes specific instances (such as specific users for Exchange email) that retention policy takes precedence over a static scope that is configured for all instances for the same location.

claims.claim: The shortest deletion period resolves policy deletion conflicts that remain after the previous precedence rules.
claims.quote: **The shortest deletion period wins.** Applicable to determine when items will be deleted from retention policies and the outcome couldn't be resolved from the previous level

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and AI apps
claims.claim: AI interaction data is retained in a hidden folder in the mailbox of the user running the app.
claims.quote: Data from generative AI messages is stored in a hidden folder in the mailbox of the user who runs the AI app.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and AI apps
claims.claim: A timer job evaluates the retained AI interactions and typically takes 1-7 days to run.
claims.quote: a timer job from the Exchange service periodically evaluates items in the hidden mailbox folder where these messages are stored. The timer job typically takes 1-7 days to run.

claims.claim: Retained content remains available for eDiscovery until it is permanently deleted.
claims.quote: Until messages are permanently deleted from the SubstrateHolds folder, they remain searchable by eDiscovery tools.

claims.where: Why it matters: meeting recordings and transcripts
claims.claim: Microsoft says Teams meeting recordings and transcripts are regularly created when using Copilot in Teams recap.
claims.quote: These files are regularly created if you're using the popular Copilot in Teams recap feature

claims.where: Why it matters: meeting recordings and transcripts
claims.claim: Meeting recordings and transcripts can automatically fall under a policy retaining all items for many years.
claims.quote: might be automatically retained with a retention policy that retains all items for many years.

claims.where: Why it matters: meeting recordings and transcripts
claims.claim: Microsoft characterizes those recording and transcript files as typically having little business value after 1-3 months.
claims.quote: these specific files typically have little business value after 1-3 months

claims.claim: Messages visible in AI apps do not accurately indicate whether the data is retained or permanently deleted for compliance.
claims.quote: Messages visible in your AI apps are not an accurate reflection of whether they are retained or permanently deleted for compliance requirements.

claims.claim: Every user benefiting from retention requires an appropriate licence, with requirements depending on the retention feature.
claims.quote: Any user benefiting from the service requires a license.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3 and Business Premium are among the plans providing rights for organization-wide, location-wide and include/exclude retention policies.
claims.quote:
For organization-wide, location-wide, or include/exclude retention policies, the following licenses provide user rights:

- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3, Business Premium

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Retention policies, adaptive-scope sentence
claims.claim: Policies with an adaptive scope need Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW or Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW.
claims.quote:
If the retention policy uses an adaptive policy scope, then one of the following licenses is required to provide user rights:

- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5
- Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW
- Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW
- Office 365 E5/A5/G5
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Policies with an adaptive scope are licensed by Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW or Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, among other listed plans.' The cited service description also permits Office 365 E5/A5/G5 and Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection and Governance; the current unqualified 'need' list incorrectly excludes them.

claims.claim: The list licensing retention label creation includes Microsoft 365 E3 and F1/F3.
claims.quote:
For retention label creation, the following licenses provide user rights:

- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3/F3/F1/Business Premium

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Retention labels, event-based retention
claims.claim: Event-based retention label settings require the narrower E5-level licensing list.
claims.quote:
Require these specific licenses to provide users rights:

- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5
- Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW
- Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW
- Office 365 E5/A5/G5

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Retention labels, disposition review
claims.claim: Disposition review requires the narrower E5-level retention label licensing list.
claims.quote:
Require these specific licenses to provide users rights:

- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5
- Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW
- Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW
- Office 365 E5/A5/G5
- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection and Governance

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Retention labels, records
claims.claim: Marking items as records requires the narrower E5-level retention label licensing list.
claims.quote:
Require these specific licenses to provide users rights:

- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5
- Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW
- Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW
- Office 365 E5/A5/G5
- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection and Governance

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Retention labels, automatic relabelling
claims.claim: Automatically changing the retention label after the retention period requires the narrower E5-level licensing list.
claims.quote:
After the retention period, automatically change the retention label,

Require these specific licenses to provide users rights:

- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5
- Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E3/E5 plus Microsoft 365 Copilot provides rights for retention policies applying to Microsoft Copilot interactions.
claims.quote:
If the retention policy applies to Microsoft Copilot interactions, the following licenses provide user rights:

- Microsoft 365 E3/E5 + Microsoft 365 Copilot

claims.claim: Priority cleanup uses the E5-level licensing list.
claims.quote:
To use the Priority cleanup policy to apply labels that bypass existing retention or eDiscovery holds, the following licenses provide user rights:

- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing must be set up to create policies including Microsoft Copilot experiences, Enterprise AI apps or Other AI apps locations.
claims.quote: You must set up pay-as-you-go billing to create retention policies that include the locations Microsoft Copilot experiences, Enterprise AI apps, and Other AI apps.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions are not charged under that pay-as-you-go requirement.
claims.quote: There's no charge for Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions.

claims.claim: The Preservation Hold library counts against the site's storage quota.
claims.quote: Because the Preservation Hold library is included in the site's storage quota, you might need to increase your storage when you use retention settings for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Retention beats deletion
claims.claim: An ordinary retention policy cannot permanently delete content preserved by an eDiscovery hold.
claims.quote: Items subject to eDiscovery hold also fall under the first principle of retention; they cannot be permanently deleted by any retention policy or retention label.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Retention beats deletion
claims.claim: Content may disappear from users' main view while permanent deletion is suspended and a retained copy remains.
claims.quote: the delete process can still be initiated (user-initiated or system-initiated) and consequently, might remove the content from users' main view. However, permanent deletion is suspended.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deletion is slow
claims.claim: Allow up to seven days for retention policy settings to apply to content.
claims.quote: When you submit retention policies for workloads and label policies to automatically apply a retention label, allow up to seven days for the retention settings to be applied to content

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deletion is slow
claims.claim: Microsoft's AI-app delete-after-one-day example can take 16 days to disappear from eDiscovery searches.
claims.quote: a delete action after 1 day could take 16 days before the message is permanently deleted so that it's no longer returned in eDiscovery searches.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Teams messages and files
claims.claim: A retention policy targeting Teams message locations does not by itself cover Teams files, meeting recordings and transcripts.
claims.quote: you should additionally configure a retention policy that includes that Microsoft 365 group by using the **Microsoft 365 Group mailboxes & sites** location. This retention policy applies to content in the group's mailbox, site, and files.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Teams messages and files
claims.claim: Meeting recordings and transcripts require the appropriate Microsoft 365 Group, SharePoint or OneDrive retention location.
claims.quote: To retain or delete Teams meeting recordings with their transcripts from user chats, you'll need a retention policy that includes the organizer's OneDrive account as the location.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Teams messages and files
claims.claim: A file can be deleted by its own retention policy while the Teams message still links to it, resulting in File not found.
claims.quote: the file still displays in the Teams message, but when users select the file, they get a "File not found" error.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Legacy Copilot coverage
claims.claim: Existing combined Teams chats and Copilot interactions policies cannot be edited once the tenant supports separate locations.
claims.quote: If you have existing retention policies for Teams chats and Copilot interactions, they continue to be supported, although they can't be edited when your tenant supports the separate locations.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Preservation Lock; controls[5].note
claims.claim: Preservation Lock is irreversible and prevents anyone, including a global administrator, from turning off the locked policy.
claims.quote: Preservation Lock locks a retention policy or retention label policy so that no one—including a global admin—can turn off the policy, delete the policy, or make it less restrictive.

claims.claim: A locked retention policy cannot be deleted.
claims.quote: No one can disable the policy or delete it

claims.claim: A locked retention policy cannot be made less restrictive.
claims.quote: a locked policy can be increased or extended, but it can't be reduced or turned off.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Preservation Lock; Open questions
claims.claim: Adaptive policy scopes currently do not support Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: Currently, adaptive policy scopes don't support Preservation Lock.

claims.claim: A tenant supports at most 1,000 retention labels.
claims.quote: A maximum of 1,000 retention labels are supported per tenant.

claims.claim: The tenant policy ceiling is 10,000 policies, subject to the stated inclusions and exclusions.
claims.quote: A single tenant can have a maximum of 10,000 policies (any configuration).

claims.claim: The 10,000-policy ceiling includes other compliance policies, rather than being exclusive to retention.
claims.quote: This maximum number includes the different policies for retention, and other policies for compliance such as policies for DLP, information barriers, eDiscovery holds, In-Place Holds, and sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents exclusions from the 10,000-policy maximum.
claims.quote:
However, this maximum excludes:

- Auto-labeling policies for SharePoint and OneDrive, unless they are for cloud attachments.

claims.claim: The Exchange policy limit is 1,800.
claims.quote: Exchange (any configuration): 1,800

claims.claim: The supported per-mailbox policy limit is 50.
claims.quote: Per mailbox: 25 is the recommended maximum before performance might be impacted; 50 is the supported limit.

claims.claim: The recommended per-mailbox maximum is 25 policies before performance might be affected.
claims.quote: Per mailbox: 25 is the recommended maximum before performance might be impacted; 50 is the supported limit.

claims.claim: The SharePoint or OneDrive limit for policies automatically covering all sites is 13.
claims.quote: SharePoint or OneDrive: (all sites automatically included): 13

claims.claim: The SharePoint or OneDrive limit for policies including or excluding specific locations is 2,600.
claims.quote: SharePoint or OneDrive (specific locations included or excluded): 2,600

claims.claim: The Exchange and SharePoint maxima are shared with other hold policies, including eDiscovery and In-Place Holds.
claims.quote: These maximum numbers for Exchange and SharePoint are not exclusive to retention but are shared with other types of hold policies that include eDiscovery holds and In-Place Holds.

claims.where: Risks and limits: One label per item
claims.claim: Only one retention label can be applied to an item at a time.
claims.quote: an item such as an email or document can have only a single retention label applied to it at a time.

claims.where: Risks and limits: One label per item
claims.claim: Retention labels do not have configurable priorities.
claims.quote: Unlike sensitivity labels, you can't configure priorities for retention labels.

claims.where: Risks and limits: One label per item
claims.claim: Retention labels do not persist when content leaves Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Retention labels, unlike sensitivity labels, don't persist if the content is moved outside Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup can override existing retention and eDiscovery holds.
claims.quote: This policy can override existing holds for retention and eDiscovery.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No administrative units
claims.claim: Retention policies for Copilots and AI apps currently do not support administrative units.
claims.quote: Currently, retention policies for Copilots and AI apps don't support administrative units.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends the Compliance Administrator role group for creating and managing retention policies and labels in data lifecycle management.
claims.quote: To grant permissions for this limited administration, we recommend that you add users to the **Compliance Administrator** admin role group.

claims.claim: A custom role group with Retention Management can be used instead.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using this default role, you can create a new role group and add the **Retention Management** role to this group.

claims.claim: View-Only Retention Management provides read-only access.
claims.quote: For a read-only role, use **View-Only Retention Management**.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup requires the Priority Cleanup Admin role.
claims.quote: admins must have the **Priority Cleanup Admin** role.

claims.claim: Compliance Administrator does not include Priority Cleanup Admin by default.
claims.quote: This role isn't included by default in the **Compliance Administrator** admin role group.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph provides POST /v1.0/security/labels/retentionLabels to create retention labels.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/labels/retentionLabels

claims.claim: The Graph create-retentionLabel API supports delegated work-or-school permissions with RecordsManagement.ReadWrite.All, not application permissions.
claims.quote:
| Delegated (work or school account) | RecordsManagement.ReadWrite.All | Not available. |
| Delegated (personal Microsoft account) | Not supported. | Not supported. |
| Application | Not supported. | Not supported. |

claims.claim: Policy lookup in the Data lifecycle management or Records management solution finds policies assigned to users, sites and Microsoft 365 groups.
claims.quote: use **Policy lookup** from the **Data lifecycle management** or **Records management** solutions in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Policy lookup requires exact email addresses or site URLs and does not accept wildcards.
claims.quote: You must specify the exact email address for a user, exact URL for a site, or exact email address for a Microsoft 365 group. You can't use wildcards, or partial matches, for example.

claims.claim: Retention label usage is shown under Data Lifecycle Management > Overview.
claims.quote: **Solutions** > **Data Lifecycle Management** > **Overview**

claims.claim: Creating, reconfiguring and deleting retention policies and labels generates audit events.
claims.quote: Administrator configuration for retention policies and retention labels is logged as auditing events when a retention policy or label is created, reconfigured, or deleted.

claims.claim: Updated retention policy has audit operation SetRetentionCompliancePolicy.
claims.quote: | Updated retention policy | SetRetentionCompliancePolicy | Administrator updated an existing a retention policy.

claims.claim: Auditing retention actions is supported for retention labels, not retention policies.
claims.quote: Retention actions that are logged as auditing events are available only for retention labels and not for retention policies:

claims.where: What to check: adaptive and static scopes
claims.claim: Adaptive scopes must be created before creating a policy that uses them.
claims.quote: If you decide to use an adaptive policy, you must create one or more adaptive scopes before you create your retention policy

claims.claim: Users assigned the Retention Management role are among the beneficiaries who need a licence.
